newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Safeway sees trial costs covered.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Safeway sees trial costs covered.

text.p: British supermarket group Safeway Plc expects costs of its trial of personalised home shopping to be covered by increased spending and a two stg charge, Ian Mumby, director of business development, said on Thursday.
"Cost of the trial will be fairly small, given the two stg charge and increased spend, that wil cover the basic costs of the trial," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.

Safeway said earlier on Thursday it would test the system, which allows customers to order basic household goods in advance and collect them at the store, on 400 loyalty card holders at its Basingstoke, southern England, store, with a second phase at its Sutton store in the summer.
Mumby said if the tests were successful and the scheme was extended, "it would be creating jobs in the future."
The scheme would allow customers to place orders on telephone lines 18 hours a day, seven days a week, and these lines are being manned by British Telecommunications (BT).
Mumby said Safeway would hope the scheme would "both increase the amount of business with existing customers and attract new customers."
He said research suggested the scheme could be "very popular" with customers.
